complexity.notes: Switching from a list comprehension to a generator inside sum() avoids an intermediate O(n) list, and starting the search at 1 removes the k==0 special case from the previous version. Both are tidy improvements; ceil(pile/k) could also be written -(-pile // k) to avoid the math import.
complexity.summary: Binary searches the eating speed k over [1, max(piles)], using an O(n) feasibility check that sums ceil(pile/k) hours across all piles and compares against h. Monotonicity of the check guarantees the first feasible k is the minimum.
